body.name: \mathcal K_{\mathrm K}
body.def: \(\mathcal K_{\mathrm K}(P_{\vartheta})\) holds when \(S=1\) almost surely and the law obeys the recursive IV-plus-proxy factorization in Figure 2(b) and equation (2) of Kawakami (2021); for each \(x\), its matrices \(A_{11,x}^{\mathrm K}\), \(A_{22,x}^{\mathrm K}\), \(A_x^{\mathrm K}(b)\), \(Q_{1,x}^{\mathrm K}\), and \(P_{1,x}^{\mathrm K}-Q_{1,x}^{\mathrm K}\) are invertible as in Theorem 1(i); the second columns of \(Q_{2,x}^{\mathrm K}(Q_{1,x}^{\mathrm K})^{-1}\) and \((P_{2,x}^{\mathrm K}-Q_{2,x}^{\mathrm K})(P_{1,x}^{\mathrm K}-Q_{1,x}^{\mathrm K})^{-1}\) differ across \(x=0,1\) as in Theorem 1(ii); and \(Y_{x,z,w}=Y_x\) and \(X_{z,w}=X_z\) as in Theorem 1(iii). Here \(P_x^{\mathrm K}\) has rows \(\bigl(1,P_{\vartheta}(Z=z_0\mid X=x)\bigr)\) and \(\bigl(P_{\vartheta}(W=w_j\mid X=x),P_{\vartheta}(W=w_j,Z=z_0\mid X=x)\bigr)\) for \(j=1,2,3\); \(Q_x^{\mathrm K}\) replaces these probabilities by their intersections with \(Y=0\); subscripts \(1,2\) select the first and last two rows; and \(A_{11,x}^{\mathrm K}\) and \(A_{22,x}^{\mathrm K}\) are the first and last \(2\times2\) diagonal blocks of \(A_x^{\mathrm K}(b)\).
body.role: exact no-selection overlap conditions of Kawakami (2021), Theorem 1
